chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Mas'ud, from Muhammad ibn Nusayr, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa: I wrote to him regarding

a group who speak and recite narrations they attribute to you and your forefathers, the contents of which repel the hearts, and it is not permissible for us to reject them as they are narrated from your forefathers (peace be upon them), nor to accept them because of what is in them … and it is a man called Ali ibn Haska, and another called al-Qasim al-Yaqtini. Among their beliefs is that they say the words of Allah the Exalted: 'Verily, Salat safeguards from indecency and wrong-doing' means a man, not prostration nor bowing. Similarly, Zakat means that man, not a set number of dirhams nor the giving out of wealth. And things among the obligations, sunnahs, and sins they have interpreted and transformed into this limit which I mentioned. So if you see fit to clarify for us and favor your followers with that in which lies their safety and salvation from these beliefs which lead them to perdition
So he (peace be upon him) wrote: This is not our religion, therefore disassociate from it.
ai.seo_question: Who are Ali ibn Haska and al-Qasim al-Yaqtini and what was their specific theological error regarding Salat and Zakat?
ai.summary: This correspondence highlights the Ghulat (extremists) sect of Ali ibn Haska and al-Qasim al-Yaqtini, who practiced ta'wil (allegorical interpretation) to reduce obligatory acts like Salat and Zakat to mere references to the Imam himself, stripping them of ritual and material substance. The Imam’s concise reply, 'This is not our religion,' serves as a definitive criterion (mizan) for distinguishing authentic Shia doctrine from their deviant theological reductions, emphasizing the necessity of adhering to both inner meaning and outer practice.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/206] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Masud from Muhammad b. Nusayr from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa who said: I wrote to him [the Imam al-Askari – the following]:

this is about a group who speak of narrations which they attribute to you and your forefathers, the contents of which repel the hearts, but it is not permissible for us to repudiate them as they are narrated on the authority of your forefathers, nor can we accept them because of what they purport … and it is a man called Ali b. Haska and another called al-Qasim al-Yaqtini. Among their beliefs is that they say the words of Allah the Elevated: “verily Salat safeguards from indecency and wrong-doing” [29:45] refers to a man [Salat is embodied in a man], not to prostration nor to bowing. Similarly, Zakat refers to that man, not to a set number of gold coins nor to the giving out of wealth. They have done likewise in regards injunctions concerning the obligatory, the recommended and the forbidden – they have interpreted and transformed it in a way akin to that which I have mentioned. So if you deem it proper to clarify for us and to favour your followers by that in which lies their safety and salvation from these beliefs which can lead them to perdition [then do so].
So he عليه السلام wrote: this is not our religion therefore disassociate from it.
